headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are exposed, but docs-only uncertainty keeps prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways from being fully ruled out.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A exposes no filesystem or MCP surface, and Agent B has no read/write filesystem, browser, subprocess, or MCP capability. With no shared communication channel documented, there is no plausible default injection path between ai-engineering-hub and LightZero.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future clipboard or file handoff between them.
Review any orchestrator wiring before enabling cross-agent messaging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, and both agents report network egress as none. Agent B cannot read files, and Agent A has no exposed I/O surfaces, so there is no documented route for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other by default.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF network egress is enabled for either agent, the data-flow assumptions no longer hold.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared sensitive workspace.
Confirm no hidden sync or export job is attached to either agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability overlap is absent: Agent A has no exposed write or shell permissions, while Agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. Without overlapping mutable-resource access, there is no write conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF Agent A is later granted filesystem or git write access, conflict risk may emerge.
IF both agents are attached to the same mutable resource, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep Agent A non-runnable or read-only.
Avoid granting Agent B write or git permissions.
Use separate directories if either agent gains write access later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is not documented, but the pairwise interaction is also not directly evidenced. Agent A is an audio-speech/open-source hub and Agent B is a game-playing engine; with no shared channel or downstream action authority shown, only an unusual orchestration that treats A’s output as authoritative would create a small blast-radius failure.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds Agent A’s outputs directly into Agent B without verification, the risk increases.
IF Agent B is configured to act on A-generated facts or instructions, cascading errors become plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step between agents.
Require schema validation on any handoff payload.
Log and diff A’s outputs before B consumes them.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. Because the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data handling, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to cite for this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, compliance review is required.
IF residency, retention, or certification requirements are introduced, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document any future data-class handling before deployment.
Add a policy check before enabling sensitive workloads.
